notes.energyAssumption: maxEnergy is 3 for every class (set in character-options.json), refilled at the start of every turn and never carried over. This is the value the costs here were originally priced against, and the value the design returned to on 2026-08-26 after a spell at 6. At 3 the player plays ~2 cards per turn against an average cost of 1.4. Enemy health must scale to that, not to the 6-energy assumption it briefly carried.
notes.scarcity: D16 removed the deck/draw. Nothing is rate-limited by a shuffle, so scarcity is authored per card via oncePerRoom and cooldown. Cards with neither are intentionally spammable and priced low.
notes.subtext: D7. Player cards, so subtext is what the CANDIDATE says. Display only — never affects resolution.
notes.types: attack | defend | power, matching the D15 starting loadout of 3 attack / 1 defend / 1 power.
notes.subtype: Left blank where nothing useful applies, per instruction.
notes.startingLoadoutRule: D15 (revised). The player does NOT pick a starting loadout. Every run begins with these five neutral cards — 3 attack, 1 defend, 1 power — regardless of class. Class cards enter the loadout later, through post-room rewards. This array is the source of truth; the game reads it rather than hardcoding ids.
notes.blockDefault: Block is 0 for every class except the Fighter (Full Stack), which resets to 1 each turn rather than to 0. Per-class values live in character-options.json under classes[].stats.startingBlock.
notes.separation: Player cards can never be used by an enemy and enemy cards can never enter a player loadout. Enforced by the `side` field — see SCHEMA.md.

cards.name: Strike

cards.subtext: I have about five years of experience with that.

cards.subtext: That's a great question.

cards.subtext: Let me walk you through a specific example.

cards.name: Deflect
cards.text: Gain 4 Block.
cards.subtext: I'd want to understand the constraints first.

cards.text: Deal 12 damage.
cards.subtext: It's actually on page two.

cards.subtext: I've done this before.

cards.name: Cold Start
cards.text: Deal 4 damage.
cards.subtext: Well — it depends.

cards.text: Deal 14 damage.
cards.subtext: Can I draw this out?

cards.name: Deep Dive

cards.subtext: Give me a second, I want to get this right.

cards.text: Your next attack this room deals double damage.
cards.subtext: Let me think about the access pattern.

cards.name: Index
cards.text: The first card you play each turn costs 0 this room.
cards.subtext: We solved that with an index.

cards.name: The Migration
cards.text: In two turns, deal 30 damage.
cards.subtext: It was a two-year migration.

cards.name: Ship It
cards.text: Deal 8 damage.
cards.subtext: I shipped it Friday.

cards.name: Both Ends
cards.text: Deal 7 damage. Gain 6 Block.
cards.subtext: I did the frontend and the backend.

cards.name: Steady Hands
cards.text: Gain 6 Block, plus 2 for each turn already taken this room.
cards.subtext: I don't panic.

cards.name: Whatever's Needed
cards.text: Copy any other card in your loadout at 60% effect.
cards.subtext: Honestly, I'll pick up whatever's needed.

cards.name: Overtime
cards.text: Deal 10 damage. Lose 3 health.
cards.subtext: I stayed late a lot, yeah.

cards.name: Full Stack
cards.text: Gain 1 additional energy each turn this room.
cards.subtext: I can cover the whole thing myself.

cards.name: Polish
cards.text: Gain 2 Flourish.
cards.subtext: I care a lot about the details.

cards.name: Pixel Perfect
cards.text: Deal 7 damage, or 10 if you already played a card this turn.
cards.subtext: Down to the pixel.

cards.name: Smoke
cards.text: Gain 8 Block. Evade the next attack entirely.
cards.subtext: That was before my time.

cards.name: The Reveal
cards.text: Deal 5 damage for each Flourish, then lose all Flourish.
cards.subtext: Actually — can I just show you the demo?

cards.name: Portfolio
cards.text: Gain 1 Flourish whenever you play a card this room.
cards.subtext: Everything's on my site if you want to look.

cards.name: App Store Review
cards.text: Deal 26 damage. Skip your next turn.
cards.subtext: We were stuck waiting on approval for nine days.

cards.name: Post-Mortem
cards.text: Gain 6 Riposte. Riposte deals its value back to any attacker.
cards.subtext: We wrote it all up afterward.

cards.name: Runbook
cards.text: Gain 9 Block.
cards.subtext: There's a runbook for that.

cards.name: On Call
cards.text: Gain 10 Riposte and 5 Block.
cards.subtext: I've been on call for three years.

cards.name: Root Cause
cards.text: Deal 12 damage, doubled if you took damage last turn.
cards.subtext: The root cause was actually upstream of us.

cards.name: Alerting
cards.text: Gain 3 Riposte at the start of each turn this room.
cards.subtext: We had alerting for exactly that.

cards.name: Blameless

cards.subtext: We do blameless post-mortems.
